name: Person Re-Identification Benchmark
description: Person re-identification (re-id) is a critical problem in video analytics applications such as security and surveillance. The public release of several datasets and code for vision algorithms has facilitated rapid progress in this area over the last few years. However, directly comparing re-id algorithms reported in the literature has become difficult since a wide variety of features, experimental protocols, and evaluation metrics are employed. In order to address this need, we present an extensive review and performance evaluation of single- and multi-shot re-id algorithms. The experimental protocol incorporates the most recent advances in both feature extraction and metric learning. To ensure a fair comparison, all of the approaches were implemented using a unified code library that includes 11 feature extraction algorithms and 22 metric learning and ranking techniques. reputation: A classic and widely used benchmark setting in person re-identification research, often used for fair cross-method comparison.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; results depend heavily on dataset and protocol, and reported scores are not directly comparable across different re-id datasets.
